(TA.) ― -b2- It is sometimes substituted for Y , when the latter letter is doubled, (K,) or is so substituted by some of the Arabs; (AA, S;) as in fuqayomij~N , for fuqayomiY~N ; (AA, S, K;) and mur~ij~N , for mur~iY~N . And in a prayer, (L,) laA yanofaEu *aA Aljad~i minoka Aljad~u The good worldly fortune of him who is possessed of such fortune will not profit him, (Mgh, L,) in the world to come, (L,) in lieu of Thee; (Mgh, L; *) i. e.,

Hence, A^ajad~aka laA tafoEalo [or A^ajad~ika ]; and, accord. to some, wajad~ika : see jid~N . ― -b2- One's lot in life; and the means of subsistence that one receives from the bounty of God. (L, K.) One says, lifulaAnK fiY h`*aA AlA^amori jad~N Such a one has in this thing, or state of affairs, means of subsistence. (A'Obeyd, L.) ― -b3- Richness; competence, or sufficiency

; or the state of being in no need, or of having no wants, or of having few wants. (S, L, Msb.) lA ynfE *A Aljd~ mnk Aljd~ , [explained above, is said to mean] Riches, &c., will not profit the possessor thereof with Thee; for nothing will profit him but acting in obedience to Thee: mnk here signifies Einodaka . (S, Msb.) ― -b4- Greatness, or majesty; (Mujáhid, S, Mgh, Msb, K;) accord. to some, specially of God: (TA:) so in the Kur lxxii. 3: (S, TA:) or his freedom from all wants or the like; syn. ginFY . (S.)
Hence, taEaAlaY jad~uka , (Mgh, TA,) in a trad. respecting prayer, (TA,) Exalted be thy greatness, or majesty. (Mgh, * TA.) ― -b5- See also A^ajad~aka , as an interrogative phrase, voce jid~N . -A2-
Also, (S, K,) and ↓ , (S, A, Mgh, K,) and ↓ , (S, Msb, K,) and ↓ , (S,) and ↓ , and ↓ , the last two with damm, (K,) applied to a man, Fortunate

; or possessed of good fortune; (S, A, Mgh, Msb;) or possessed of good worldly fortune: (TA:) or possessing great fortune, or great good fortune: (K:) [the words here given from the S are there coupled with synonyms of the same form, thus; ↓ HaZiyZN , and maHoZuwZN ↓ , and jad~N HaZ~u , and HaZ~iY~N ↓ ; on the authority of ISk:] ↓ , with damm, as an epithet applied to a man, is said by Sb to be syn. with majoduwdN ; and its pl. is jud~Nwna only. (L.) -A3- Also jad~u , A grandfather; the father's father, and the mother's father: (S, Msb, K:) and (assumed tropical:) a higher ascendant; an ancestor: (Msb:) and ↓ a grandmother; the father's mother, and the mother's mother: (K:) [and (assumed tropical:) a female ancestor: ] pl. of the former, A^ajodaAdN [a pl. of pauc.] and juduwdN and juduwdap
Hence, accord. to some, wajad~ika laA tafoEalo : see jid~N . -A4- See also jud~apN : ― -b2- and see jadiydN .

: see jad~N , in two places. -A2- See also jud~apN . ― -b2- Also The side ( jaAnib ) of anything. (K.) -A3- And A well in a place where is much herbage, or pasture: (S, Msb, K:) a well abounding with water; (K;) [and] so ↓ ; (KL;) but A'Obeyd says that this is not known: (L:) and, contr., a well containing little water: a scanty water, or water little in quantity: a water at the extremity of a [ desert such as is called ] falaAp : (K:) an old water: (Th, K:) an old well: (KL:) pl. (in all these senses, TA) A^ajodaAdN . (Msb, TA.)
[accord. to some an inf. n., but accord. to others a simple subst., (see jad~a ,)] Seriousness, or earnestness, contr. of hazolN , (S, A, Msb, K,) in speech. (Msb.)

Hence, valaAvN jid~uhun~a jid~N wahazoluhun~a jid~N [There are three things in relation to which what is serious is serious and what is jesting is serious ]: a saying of Mohammad, whereby he forbade a man's divorcing and emancipating and marrying and then retracting, saying “ I was jesting; ” as was customary in the time of paganism. (Msb.) A^ajid~aka and ↓ signify the same; (S;) but the former is the more chaste; (TA;) jid~ and jad~ being thus used only as prefixed nouns: (S, K:) As says that the meaning is, A^abijid~K minoka h`*aA [ Does this proceed from thee in seriousness, or in earnest? ]; and that jid~ is put in the accus. case because of the rejection of the [prep.] b : AA says that the meaning is, maA laka A^ajid~FA minoka [ What aileth thee? Doth it proceed from thee in seriousne

; or the phrase may be originally Ajd~k A^ano laA tafoEala , An being suppressed, and its government annulled: [therefore it may be rendered, in the former case, Is it with seriousness on thy part, thou doing such a thing? and in the latter case, Is it with seriousness on thy part that thou will not do such a thing? i. e. dost thou mean seriously that thou will not do it? or in this case, Ajd~k may be used as a form of adjuration in one of the senses explained above, and laA tafoEalu may mean, that thou do not such a thing

; or Ajd~k may mean wajad~aka , (explained above, and so in the three exs. below,) and laA tafoEalu , thou wilt not do it:] and, as AHei says, there is here a nice point, which is this; that the noun [meaning the pronoun] to which jd~ is prefixed should agree in person with the verb which follows it; so that one should say, Ajd~iY laA A^ukorimuka , and Ajd~ka laA tafoEalu , and Ajd~hu laA yazuwrunaA ; because jd~ is an inf. n. corroborating the proposition that follows it. (MF.) ― -b2-

Also, [and in this case, likewise, accord. to some an inf. n., but accord. to others a simple subst., (see, again, jad~a ,)] A striving, labour, or toil; exertion of one's self, or of one's power or efforts or endeavours or ability; vigorousness, strenuousness, laboriousness, diligence, studiousness, sedulousness, earnestness, or energy; painstaking, or extraordinary painstaking; (S, L, Msb, K;) in affairs, (S,) or in an affair. (Msb, K.)

Hence, jid~FA [meaning In a great, or an extraordinary, degree; greatly, much, exceedingly, or extraordinarily; very; very greatly, or very much; extremely ]; as in the phrase, (Msb,) fulaAnN muHosinN jid~FA [ Such a one is beneficent in a great, or an extraordinary, degree; very, exceedingly, or extremely, beneficent ]: you should not say jad~FA . (S, Msb. * [In my copy of the Msb, it is mHsn jd~A bAlftH : but the context shows that there is an omission here, and that, after jd~A , we should read, as in the S, walaA taqulo jad~FA .]) jid~FA [in a phrase of this kind] is put in the accus. case as an inf. n. [of which the verb is understood; so that, in the ex. given above, the proper meaning is, yajid~u fiY AlA_iHosaAni jid~FA striving in beneficence with a great striving ]; because it is
: see jad~N , near the end of the paragraph.

The bank, or side, or a river; as also jid~apN and ↓ (IAth, L, K) and ↓ (IAth, Mgh, L) and ↓ , (Mgh, L, K,) accord. to some, but correctly jud~N ; so called because cut off from the river, or because cut by the water, in like manner as it is called saAHilN because it is abraded by the water: (Mgh:) or the part of a river that is near the land; as also ↓ : (L:) and the shore of the sea: (MF:) accord. to As, jd~p is an arabicized word from the Nabathean kd~ . (L.) ― -b2- The stripe, or streak, that is on the back of the ass, differing from his general colour. (S, A, * K.) And (tropical:) A streak (Fr, S, K, TA) in anything, (TA,) as in a mountain, (Fr, S,) differing in colour from the rest of the mountain, (S,) white and black and red; (Fr, TA;) as also in the sky: (A, TA:) pl. judadN , (Fr,

Hence, app., but accord. to the S from the same word as signifying “a streak,”] rakiba jud~apF mina AlA^amori , (S, A, TA,) or jud~apa AlA^amori , (K,) (tropical:) He set upon a way, or manner, of performing the affair: (A:) or he formed an opinion respecting the affair, or case. (Zj, S, A, K.) ― -b6- See also jid~apN .
: see jud~apN , in two places: ― -b2- and see jadiydN . ― -b3- Also A rag

; or piece torn off from a garment; and so ↓ : thus in the saying, maA Ealayohi jid~apN and jud~apN [ There is not upon him a rag ]. (K.) ― -b4- A collar upon the neck of a dog: (Th, L, K:) pl. judadN [like luHFY pl. of liHoyapN , or perhaps a mistake for jidadN ]. (L.)

Hard ground: (S:) or hard level ground: (Har p. 522:) [see also jadojadN :] or rough level ground: (K:) or rough ground: or level ground: (TA:) or a level and spacious tract of land; a tract such as is called SaHoraA=' , and such as is called faDaA=' , containing no soft place in which the feet sink, nor any mountain, nor any [ hill such as is called ] A^akamap ; sometimes wide, and sometimes of little width: (ISh:) [and] a conspicuous road: (Bd in xxxv. 25:) pl. A^ajodaAdN . (ISh.) It is said in a prov., mano salaka Aljadada A^amina AlEivaAra [ He who walks along hard, or hard and level, ground is secure from stumbling ]; (S, TA;) meaning, he who pursues the course marked out by common consent is secure from stumbling. (TA.) And makaAnN jadadN occurs in a trad., meaning Level ground. (TA.

and ↓ The cutting off of the fruit of palm-trees. (S, * A, * L, Msb, * K. *) You say, h`*aA zamanu AljadaAdi and AljidaAdi [ This is the time, or season, of the cutting off of the fruit of the palmtrees ]. (S, A, Msb. *) Some say that jdAd signifies particularly [as above,] the cutting off [of the fruit] of palm-trees; and j*A* , the cutting off of all fruits, in a general sense: others say that they signify the same. (TA.) ― -b2- Also The time, or season, of the cutting off of the fruit of palm-trees. (S, * L.) You say jadaAdN and jidaAdN , like SaraAmN and SiraAmN , and qaTaAfN and qiTaAfN ; (Ks, S;) whence it seems as though the measures faEaAlN and fiEaAlN were uniformly applicable to every noun signifying the time of the action; such nouns being likened to A^awaAnN and A_iwaAnN . (S.)
: see jadaAdN , and jaAd~N .

, (ISk, S, A, K,) or jaduwdapN , (L,) Having little milk, (ISk, S,) or not from any imperfection; (L;) applied to a ewe, (ISk, S, K,) but not to a she-goat; the epithet maSuwrN being used in the latter case: (ISk, S:) or a ewe or she-goat having no milk; as also ↓ : (A:) pl. jadaAy^idu (S, L) and jidaAdN . (L.) ― -b2- Also A fat she-ass: pl. jidaAdN . (AZ, K.)

, of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , [i. e. ↓ ,] Cut, or cut off. (S, Msb.) A poet says, A^abiY Hub~iY sulayomaY A^ano yabiydaA waA^amosaY HaboluhaA xalaqFA jadiydaA [ My love of Suleymà hath refused to perish; but her cord (i. e. her tie of affection to me) hath become worn out and cut ]: (S:) [as jdyd signifies “new” more commonly than "cut,"] this verse appears as though it involved a contradiction. (MF.) ― -b2- Applied to a garment, or a piece of cloth [sufficient for a garment or the like], Newly cut off [ from the web ] by the weaver: (S, K:) and so (without p , S) applied to a miloHafap ; (S, A;) thus applied to a fem. n. because syn. with ↓ ; (S, ISd;) or, accord. to Sb, because by mlHfp in this case is meant A_izaAr , and for a like reason in like cases
What is cut off from the roots, or eradicated, of, or from, palm-trees &c. (Lh, TA.)

The kind of pad, or stuffed thing, ( rifaAdapN ,) and the felt, stuck, or attached, beneath the two boards of a horse's saddle: there are two such things, called jadiydataAni : (S:) or the jdydtAn consist of the felt that is stuck, or attached, in the inner side of a horse's and of a camel's saddle: (L:) but jdydp thus applied is a post-classical word: the [classical] Arabs say jadoyapN , (S,) or, as in J's own handwriting, jadiy~apN . (So in the margin of a copy of the S.) -A2- See also jud~apN .
: see jad~N , in two places.
Hard level ground: (S, K:) [see also jadadN :] smooth ground: and rough ground: (TA:) a smooth tract such as is called fayof . (AA, TA.)

[The cricket; ] i. q. Sar~aAru All~ayoli , (S, M,) a small flying thing, (K,) that leaps, or springs, or bounds, much, (S, M,) and creaks by night, (TA,) and bears a resemblance to the jaraAd [or locust ]: (S, M, K:) and a certain insect like the junodab , (M, L, K,) except that it is generally blackish, and short, but in some instances inclining to white; also called SaroSarN : (M, L:) or i. q. SadFY and junodabN : (El-'Adebbes:) pl. jadaAjidu . (S.) Accord. to IAar, A certain insect that clings to a skin, or hide, and eats it. (TA.) -A2- See also jud~N .

act. part. n. of jad~a ; (Mgh, L;) Cutting, or cutting off. (Mgh.) -A2- A^ajaAd~u A^anota A^amo haAzilN Art thou serious or jesting? (A.) It is said in a trad., laA yaA^oxu*an~a A^aHadukumo mataAEa A^axiyhi laAEibFA jaAd~FA [ By no means shall any one of you take the property of his brother in play and in earnest ]; by which is meant taking a thing without meaning to steal it, but meaning to vex and anger the owner, so that the taker is in play with respect to theft, but in earnest in annoying. (TA in art. lEb .) ― -b2- fulaAnN jaAd~N Such a one is striving, labouring, or toiling; exerting himself or his power or efforts or endeavours or ability; &c. (TA.) And ↓ , thus with the two similar words together, (As, S, L,) signifies the same [in an intensive degree]. (L, TA.) -A3- jaAd~u miAy^ap

The main part of a road; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) its middle: (Mgh, Msb, and M voce jarajap :) or its even part: or the beaten track, or part along which one walks, or travels; the conspicuous part thereof: or a main road that comprises other roads, or tracks, and upon which one must pass: (TA:) or a road, or way, absolutely; as also ↓ : (Zj, MF:) or a road leading to water: (AHn, TA:) it is so called because it is marked with tracks, forming lines: (T, TA:) pl. jawaAd~N , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) occurring in poetry without teshdeed, but disapproved by As. (L.) fulaAnN EalaY AljaAd~api means (assumed tropical:) Such a one is following the right course of action or the like. (Mgh.) You say also, huwa EalaY jaAd~api AlHaq~i (assumed tropical:) [ He is on the road, or main road, of truth ]: not, howeve

[ Having some part, or parts, cut, or cut off: fem. jad~aA='u ]. ― -b2- [Hence,] jad~aA='u A ewe, or she-goat, or she-camel, (TA,) having her ear cut off. (K, TA.) ― -b3- A ewe, or she-goat, having her teats cut off; (Sh, TA;) as also ↓ [q. v.], applied to a she-camel: (As, TA:) or having her udder cut off. (Khálid, TA.) ― -b4- [And hence,] (assumed tropical:) A milch animal (TA [in the S app. restricted to a ewe]) whose milk has passed away, (ISk, S, K,) by reason of some fault, or imperfection: (ISk, S:) see also jaduwdN : or a ewe, or she-camel, or she-ass, having little milk; having a dry udder: or having dry teats, being hurt by the SiraAr [q. v.]: (L:) and A^ajad~u (assumed tropical:) a breast that has become dry. (AHeyth.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) A woman small in the breast: (S,

A she-camel having her teats cut off in consequence of injury occasioned to her by the SiraAr [q. v.]. (S.) See also A^ajad~u . -A2- And mujad~adN A [garment of the kind called] kisaA=' having stripes of different colours. (S.)

: see jaAd~N . ― -b2- A_in~ahaA lmjd~p biAlr~ajuli , a phrase mentioned by As, said of a she-camel, meaning, Verily she is quick in her pace with the man: but Az says, I know not whether he said ↓ or mujid~apN : the former would be from jad~a ; and the latter, from A^ajad~a . (L.)

senses.text: 1 , (A, Msb, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. juduwbapN , (S, A, Msb, K,) It (a place, S, A, K, or a country, or region, Msb,) was, or became, affected with drought, barrenness, or dearth

; or with drought, and dryness of the earth; (S, A, Msb, K;) as also jadiba , (A,) inf. n. jadabN ; (KL;) or jadaba ; (K;) and ↓ ; (A, K;) or jadibat , aor. ; and ↓ ; both said of the earth or land ( AlA^aroD ): (Msb:) and ↓ AlbilaAdu the countries, or regions, were affected with drought, and the prices became high [ therein ]. (TA.) -A2- jadabahu , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) aor. (M, Msb, K) and , (K,) inf. n. jadobN , (Msb,) He found fault with it; dispraised it; expressed disapprobation of it. (S, M, A, Msb, K.) So in the saying (S, A) relating to 'Omar, (A, TA,) in a trad., (S,) jadaba Als~amara baEoda AlEi$aA='i (S) or baEoda AlEatamapi (A) [ He expressed disapprobation of night-discourse after nightfall, or after the first third of the night reckoned from the disappearance of the redness of

3 , (ISk, S, A, TA,) inf. n. mujaAdabapN , (TA,) The camels experienced, or have experienced, drought, and barrenness, or dryness of the earth, this year, and have become in such a state as not to eat anything but dry and black herbage, dry vumaAm [or panic grass ]: (ISk, S, TA:) or have not met with, or found, anything but what was bad, by reason of drought, and barrenness, or dryness of the earth, this year. (A.)
4 see 1, in three places. ― -b2- A^ajodabati Als~anapu The year became one of drought, barrenness, or dearth
; or drought, and dryness of the earth. (A, * TA.) ― -b3- Ajdb Alqawomu The people, or company of men, experienced drought, barrenness, or death

; or drought, and dryness of the earth. (S, A, Msb, K.) ― -b4- [Hence,] nazalonaA bibaniY fulaAnK faA^ajodabonaA (tropical:) We alighted as guests at the abode of the sons of such a one, and found not entertainment with them, though they were in the enjoyment of plenty: (A:) [or] nazalonaA fulaAnFA faA^ajoabonaAhu (assumed tropical:) we alighted as guests at the abode of such a one, and [ found that ] he did not entertain us. (TA.) [The latter, if correct, is from what next follows.] -A2- Ajdb AlA^aroDa He found the land to be affected with drought, barrenness, or dearth
; or with drought, and dryness of the earth. (S, A, K.)
5 (assumed tropical:) I do not deem it disagreeable, or unsuitable, to accompany thee; syn. maA A^asotawoximu . (K.)

Drought, barrenness, or dearth; contr. of xiSobN ; (S;) i. q. maHolN , (A, Msb, K,) i. e. drought, or suspension of rain, and dryness of the earth; (Msb;) dryness and barrenness of the earth: (Har p. 576:) and ↓ is a name, or subst., for AljadobN , (K, TA,) meaning AlmaHolu ; as in the saying of the rájiz, cited by Sb, laqado xa$iytu A^ano A^araY jidab~aA fiY EaAminaA baEoda maA A^axoSab~aA [ Verily I feared to see drought, or barrenness, &c., in this our year, after it had been abundant in herbage ]; jidab~aA being used for AljadobaA
; or, accord. to one reading, it is ↓ , with a doubled b added; the change being made for the sake of the metre. (M, TA. [Respecting A^axoSab~aA , see
4 in art. xSb .]) ― -b2- Also A place, (S, A, K,) or a country, or region, (Msb,) affected with drought, barrenness, or dearth

; or with drought, and dryness of the earth; and so ↓ (S, A, Msb, K) and ↓ and ↓ , (K,) the last derived from judiba though this verb has not been used, (TA,) and ↓ , (M, A,) of which the pl. is majaAdiybu . (A.) You say also A^aroDN jadobN [in which jdb is an inf. n. (though app. obsolete as such) and therefore applicable to a fem. subst.] (ISd, TA) and jadobapN (S, A, Msb, K) and ↓ (A, Msb) and ↓ (Msb) and ↓ (Lh, M, Msb) and ↓ , of which last the pl. is majaAdiybu , (Msb,) A land affected with drought, &c.: (S, M, A, &c.:) and A^aroDuwna juduwbN , (S, K,) as though to each part were applied the term jadobN [used as a subst.] from which is formed the pl. juduwbN , (TA,) and jadobN , (K,) which is here an inf. n. used as an epithet [and therefore applicable to a pl. subst.], (TA,) lands af
: see ja*abaAt , in art. j*b .
and jadobab~N : see jadobN .
: see jadobN , in three places.

Finding fault, dispraising, expressing disapprobation: whence the saying of Dhu-rRummeh, fayaA laka mino xad~K A^asiylK w manoTiqK raxiymK wamino xaloqK taEal~ala jaAdibuho meaning [ O thou smooth and even cheek, and gentle speech, and make ] whereof he who dispraises it occupies himself vainly, finding no defect in it. (S, TA.) ― -b2- It is also said [as in the K &c.] to signify Lying; and the author of the 'Eyn says that it has no verb belonging to it [in this sense]; but this is a mistranscription [for xaAdibN ]: AZ says that jaAdibN , with j , has the signification here first given. (M, TA.)

and junodubN (S, K, &c.) and jinodabN , like dirohamN , (Sb, M, K,) the last of which is of weakest authority, because of a rare measure, whereof it has been said that there are only four examples: (TA:) in all of them the n is said by some to be radical; but others, with more reason, hold it to be augmentative: (MF:) Sb says that it is augmentative: (S:) A species of locust, (S, K,) well known: (K:) or the male locust: or small locust: or, accord. to Seer, i. q. SadFY [ a kind of cricket ], that creaks by night, and hops and flies: [but see SadFY :] or, accord. to the M, it is smaller than the SdY , and is found in the deserts: pl. janaAdibu . (TA.) Sr~ Aljndb [i. e. Sar~a Aljunodabu The jndb creaked ] is a saying of the Arabs, used as a proverb; alluding to a difficult affair by which a

[ i. q. jadobN as syn. with jadiybN : fem. jadoyaA='u . Hence,] falaApN jadoyaA='u : see jadobN . ― -b2- [Hence also,] sanapN jadobaA='u A year of much snow. (L in art. $hb .) ― -b3- A^ajodabu is [also] said in the M to be [used as] a subst. applied to what is termed mujodib [i. e. as syn. with the latter word used as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant; app. meaning A place, or the like, affected with drought, &c.]. (TA.) ― -b4- [
Also, as a comparative and superlative epithet, meaning More, and most, affected with drought, &c.; contr. of A^axoSabu .]

, in a trad., where it is said, wakaAnato fiyhi A^ajaAdibu A^amosakati AlmaA='i , (K, * TA,) or wkAnt fiyhaA , (TA,) [ And there were in it AjAdb that retained the water ], is said to be pl. of A^ajodubN , which is pl. of ↓ , (K, TA,) like as A^akaAlibu is pl. of A^akolubN , which is pl. of kalobN ; (TA;) and signifies hard parts of the ground, that retain water, and do not imbibe it quickly

; or, as some say, land having no plants or herbage, from ↓ meaning “ drought ” &c: the word is thus written in the two Saheehs, of El-Bukháree and Muslim: (IAth, TA:) but some say that it is an anomalous pl. of jadobN , like as maHaAsinu is of HusonN : and there are other readings; namely, A^ajaA*ibu and A^aHaAdibu and A^aHaAzibu and A^ajaAridu , pl. of A^ajoradu , and A_ixaA*aAtN , pl. of A_ixaA*apN . (MF, TA.)
, and its fem., with p : see jadobN .
Land scarely ever, or never, abundant in herbage, or in the goods, conveniences, or comforts, of life; scarcely ever, or never, fruitful, or plentiful. (K.)

senses.text: 8 He made, or prepared, a jadav , i. e., a grave, or sepulchre
; or did so for himself. (S, K, TA.)

A grave; a sepulchre; pl. A^ajodaAvN (S, Msb, K) and A^ajoduvN ; (S, K;) of which latter, J cites an ex., but in this instance it is the proper name of a place. (TA.) It is of the dial. of Tihámeh: the people of Nejd say jadafN : (Msb:) or [as some say] the f in the latter is a substitute for the v in the former; for AjdAv is used as a pl. by common consent, and AjdAf is not used: (TA:) but Suh affirms, in the R, that the latter pl. is used by Ru-beh. (TA in art. jdf .)

(MF on the letter d .) You say, jaladahu AlHad~a , inf. n. as above, He inflicted upon him the flogging ordained by the law. (S, L.) ― -b2- jaladati AlHay~apu The serpent bit: (K:) or, accord. to some, one says of the serpent called A^asowadu , specially, yajolidu bi*anabihi [ it strikes with its tail ]. (TA.) ― -b3- jalada jaAriyatahu , (K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) He lay with his young wo

572.) ― -b4- jalada bihi AlA^aroDa He smote the ground with him; (TA;) he threw him down prostrate on the ground. (A, TA.) (TA.) kunotu A^ata$ad~adu fayujoladu biY , in a trad., means [ I used to exert my strength, or energy, but ] sleep would overcome me so that I fell down. (L.) ― -b5- jaladahu EalaY AlA^amori (tropical:) He compelled him against his will to do the thing. (A, K.) ― -b6- yujoladu bikul~i xayorK (or, as related by AHát, yjl* , with * , TA) (tropical:) He is imagined to possess every good quality. (A, K.) But the saying of EshSháfi'ee kaAna mujaAlidN yujoladu means (assumed tropical:) Mujálid used to be pronounced a liar, (K, TA,) or suspected and accused of lyin

2 , (IAar, T, S, Mgh,) inf. n. tajoliydN , (T, S, Mgh, K,) He skinned a camel (IAar, T, S, Mgh, K) that had been slaughtered: (S, K:) one seldom uses salaxa thus [in relation to a camel]. (S.) ― -b2- Also He covered a thing with skin; as, for instance, a pair of socks, or stockings: (Mgh:) and in like manner, [ he bound ] a book: (A, K: *) and he clad a young camel in the skin of another young camel: (L: [see jaladN :]) thus the verb bears two contr. significations. (Mgh.) -A2- [ He ordered to be flogged. (Freytag's Lex.: but without any indication of an authority.)] -A3- [ He, or it, rendered a man hardy, strong, sturdy, and enduring, or patient: so in the present day.]

You say, jAldhu biAls~ayofi , (L,) inf. n. mujaAladapN (S, A, L) and jilaAdN , (A, L,) He contended with him in fight with the sword. (S, * A, L.) And jAldwA biAls~uyuwfi , (K, TA,) and ↓ (S, A, L, and so in the CK instead of jAldwA ) bAlsywf , (S,) and ↓ , (S, A, L,) They contended, one with another, in fight with swords. (S, A, * L, K.) ― -b2- [See also HaADarahu .]

4 (assumed tropical:) He constrained, compelled, or necessitated, him to have recourse to, or betake himself to, him, or it: (so in some copies of the K:) or he made him to stand in need of, or to want, him, or it. (AA, L, and so in some copies of the K and in the TA.) -A2- A^ajoladati AlA^aroDu [or A^ujolidat ]: and A^ujoliduwA : see

(S, * A, * L, K. *) So in the phrase tjl~d lil$~aAmitiyna [ He constrained himself to behave with hardiness, &c., to those who rejoiced at his misfortune ]. (A, TA.) In the phrase tjl~d Eanohu [ He constrained himself to endure with hardiness and patience the loss, or want, of him, or it ], the verb is made trans. by means of En because it implies the meaning of taSab~ara . (L.) ― -b2- Also He feigned, or made a show of, hardiness, strength, sturdiness, and endurance, or patience. (L.)
3. -A2- Ajtld AlA_inaA='a , (AZ, TA,) or maAfiY AlA_inaA='i , (K,) He drank all that was in the vessel; (AZ, K, TA;) as also AHtld . (AZ, TA.)

(sometimes pronounced jaDodN , S) and ↓ , (applied to a man, S, A, Mgh,) Hardy, strong, sturdy, (S, * A, * L, K, *) and enduring, or patient: (L:) not baliyd [q. v.]: (Mgh:) pl. [of either] julodN , (S, L, K,) or juludN , (so in some copies of the K,) and juladaA='u and A^ajolaAdN [a pl. of pauc.] (S, L, K) and jilaAdN . (K.) And [the fem.] jalodapN A hardy and strong she-camel; strong to labour and to journey; that heeds not the cold: and also swift: pl. jalodaAtN : (L:) and a she-camel that yields a copious flow of milk: (Th, TA:) sing. of jilaAdN , (S,) which signifies she-camels abounding with milk; as also majaAliydu , (K,) pl. of ↓ ; (TA;) or she-camels having neither milk nor young: (K:) [see also jaladN :] or she-camels that yield the most greasy, or unctuous, sort of milk: and so

, (S, Msb, K, &c.,) the only form of the word mentioned by the generality of the lexicographers; (TA;) occurring at the end of a verse with kesr to the second as well as the first letter, ↓ , agreeably with a license allowed to a poet in such a case, to give to a quiescent letter in a rhyme the same vowel as that which the preceding letter has; (S;) and ↓ , (IAar, S, K,) like $ibohN and $abahN , and mivolN and mavalN ; but this is said by ISk to be unknown; (S;) The skin of any animal; (K;) the integument of the body and limbs of an animal: (Az, Msb:) or the exterior of the ba$arapN [or upper skin ] of an animal: (Msb: [but this is a strange explanation:]) pl. juluwdN (S, Msb, K) and (sometimes, Msb) A^ajolaAdN [a pl. of pauc.]. (Msb, K.) ― -b2- [The pl.] A^ajolaAdN signifies also, and ↓ l

: see jilodN . ― -b2- Also The skin of a camel, or other beast, with which another beast is clothed: (L:) the skin of a young camel, which ( being stripped off, S) is put over the body of another young camel, in order that the mother of the skinned young one ( smelling it, S) may conceive an affection for it [ and suckle it ]: (S, K:) or the skin of a young camel, which is stuffed with panic grass ( vumaAm ), (K, TA,) or some other plant, (TA,) and put before a she-camel, in order that she may be induced thereby to affect that which is not her young one [ and so yield her milk ], (K, TA,) or, to affect the young one of another. (L, TA.) -A2- A ewe or she-goat whose young one dies at the time of her bringing it forth; as also ↓ : pl. [of the former] jilaAdN and [of the latter] jaladaAtN . (

Also, [as a coll. gen. n.,] Great she-camels, having neither young ones nor milk; n. un. with p : (S:) [see also jalodN :] or great camels, among which are no little ones; (K;) n. un. with p : (TA:) and (app. as a quasipl. n., TA) sheep or goats, and camels, having neither young ones nor milk; (K;) app. meaning having no little ones to which they give such: (Mohammad Ibn-El-Mukarram, TA:) or she-camels having no young ones with them, so that they endure patiently the heat and cold: (Fr, TA:) or she-camels having no milk, and the young ones of which have gone away from them; including what are called banaAtu All~abuwni , and such as are above these in age; and also such as are called maxaASN , and Ei$aArN , and HiyaAlN ; but when they have given birth to their young, they cease to be termed
Also, as a subst. or an inf. n., (L, [see jaluda ,]) Hardiness, strength, sturdiness, (S, * A, * L, K, *) and endurance, or patience. (T.)

a more particular term than jilodN ; (S, L;) signifying A piece, or portion, of skin. (L.) ― -b2- One says also jilodapu AlEayoni [app. meaning The eyelid ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And qawomN mino jilodatinaA A people, or company of men, of ourselves, and of our kinsfolk. (TA.) -A2- See also jalodN .
: see jaladN , in three places.

A woman flogged with a whip; as also with p : pl. jalodaY and jalaAy^idu : (Lh, L:) the former pl. thought by ISd to be of the former sing.; and the latter, of the latter. (L.) -A2- Hoarfrost, or rime; i. e. dew that falls (S, A, K) from the sky (S) upon the ground (S, A, K) and congeals; (S, K;) also called DariybN and saqiyTN ; (S;) like SaqiyEN . [dim. of jilodapN ] One of the TabaqaAt [ coats, or tunics, ] of the eye. (TA.)
[ A dealer in skins; ] a rel. n. from juluwdN , pl. of jilodN . (TA.)

: see jaladN , in two places.
: see jilodN , in two places.

senses.text: 1 , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , (A, K,) inf. n. juluwsN (S, A, Msb, K) and ↓ , (S, A, K,) He placed his seat, or posteriors, upon rugged [or rather elevated ] ground, such as is termed jalosN : this is the primary signification: (TA:) [and hence,] He sat; i. q. qaEada [when the latter is used in its largest sense]: (Msb, and so S and L and A and K in art. qEd :) you say, jalasa mutarab~iEFA and qaEada mutarab~iEFA [ He sat cross-legged ]: (Msb:) accord. to El-Fárábee and others, contr. of qaAma ; and thus it has a more common application than qaEada [when the latter is used in its most proper and restricted sense]: (Msb:) but qaEada also signifies the contr. of qaAma : ('Orweh Ibn-Zubeyr, L in art. qEd :) properly speaking, jalasa differs from qaEada ; the former signifying he sat up
; or sat after sleeping, or prostration, (Msb,) or after lying on his side; (B, TA;) and the latter, he sat down

; or sat after standing: (Msb, B, TA: and see other authorities to the same effect in art. qEd :) for juluwsN is a change of place from low to high, and quEuwdN is a change of place from high to low: and one says, jalasa mut~akiy^FA , but not qaEada mut~akiy^FA , meaning [ He sat ] leaning, or reclining, upon one side: (Msb:) but both these verbs sometimes signify he was, or became: and thus, [it is said,] jalasa mutarab~iEFA and faEada mutarab~iEFA signify he was, or became, cross-legged: and jalasa bayona $uEabihaA AlA^arobaEi in like manner signifies he was, or became, [ between her four limbs, ] (El-Fárábee, Msb,) because the man, in this case, is resting upon his own four limbs. (Msb.) [ jalasa maEahu and jalasa A_ilayohi , like xalaA mEh and xlA Alyh , signify the same; i. e. He sat
Also, (aor. , inf. n. jalosN , TA,) He came to Aljalos , (TA,) or [ the high country called ] Nejd: (T, S, A, TA:) and in like manner said of a cloud; it came to Nejd. (TA.)

3 , inf. n. mujaAlasapN and jilaAsN , [ He sat with him. ] (TA.) You say, laA tujaAliso mano laA tujaAniso [ Sit not with him with whom thou wilt not be congenial ]. (A, TA.) And kariymu Aln~iHaAsi Tay~iybu AljilaAsi [ Generous in origin, or disposition; pleasant to sit with; ] is said of a man. (TA.)
4 [ He seated him; made him to sit: or he made him to sit up ]: (S, K, TA:) he gave him place, or settled him, ( mak~anahu ,) in sitting. (TA.)
6 [ They sat together; one with another; ] (S, A, TA;) fiY AlmajaAlisi [ in the sittingplaces ]. (S.)

10 [ He asked him, or desired him, to sit: or to sit up. ]. You say, raA=niY qaAy^imFA faA@sotajolasaniY [ He saw me standing, and he asked me, or desired me, to sit ]: (A, TA:) but this is at variance with what we have mentioned in the beginning of the art., respecting the distinction [between jalasa and qaEada ]. (TA.)
Rugged ground or land: (S, K:) this is the primary signification. (TA.) ― -b2- [
Also, app., Elevated ground or land:] a place elevated and hard: or, as some say, a tract of land extending widely. (Ham p.

688.) ― -b3- [And hence,] Aljalosu What is elevated above the gawor [or low country ]: (TA:) applied especially to the country of Nejd. (T, S, M, K.) -A2- [Persons sitting: or sitting up: ] a quasi-pl. n., accord. to Sb, or a pl., accord. to Akh, of ↓ : said to be used as sing. and pl. and fem. and masc.; but this assertion is of no account: (ISd, L:) or the people of a majolis : (Lh, ISd, L, K:) [↓ is also a pl. of ↓ ; like as bukiY~N , originally bukuwYN , is of baAki : or it is an inf. n. used as an epithet: see jaAvK :)] you say qawomN juluwsN [ a company of men sitting: or sitting up ]. (S.) [See also majolisN .] ― -b2- Also A woman who sits in the finaA=' [or court of the house ], not quitting it: (K:) or she who is of noble rank (K, TA) among her people. (TA.)
: see jaliysN , in two places.
A single sitting: or sitting up. (Msb.)
A mode or manner, (TA,) kind, (Msb,) or state, (S, A, Msb,) of sitting: or of sitting up. (S, * A, * Msb, K. *) You say, huwa Hasanu Aljilosapi [ He has a good mode, &c., of sitting ]. (A, Msb, K.)
A man (S) who sits much; sedentary. (S, K.)

(S, A, Msb, K) and ↓ (TA, as found in a copy of the K, [but this is an intensive form,]) and ↓ (S, A, K) A companion with whom one sits: (A, Msb, K:) fem. of the first with p : (TA:) and pl. [of the same] julasaA='u (A, K) and [irreg., being by rule pl. of jaAlisN ,] jul~aAsN . (K.) You say, ↓ and jaliysiY [ He is my companion with whom I sit ]; like as you say, huwa xidoniY and xadiyniY . (S.)
: see jaliysN .

: see jalosN , in two places. ― -b2- Also A man, and a cloud, coming to [ the high country called ] Nejd. (TA.) You say, raA^ayotuhumo yaEoduwna jaAlisiyna I saw them running, coming to Nejd. (A, TA.)
: see 1: ― -b2- and see majolisN .

A sitting-place; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ with p ; (Fr, Lh, Sgh, K;) similar to makaAnN and makaAnapN : (Sgh, TA:) [ a place where persons sit together and converse; a sitting-room: ] a thing upon which one sits: (MF:) some make a strange distinction between majolisN and ↓ , asserting the former to be applied to the chamber or house ( bayot ) [ in which people sit ]; and the latter, to a place of honour upon which it is forbidden to sit without permission; but the former is the only correct form of the two: (MF, TA:) pl. majaAlisu . (S, Msb.) You say, Aurozuno fiY majolisika and ↓ [ Be thou grave ] in thy sitting-place. (Fr, Sgh.) ― -b2- (tropical:) The people of a majolis ; (Msb, TA;) elliptical, for A^aholu majolisK : (TA:) an assembly, or a company of men, sitting [ together ]: (Th, TA:)
146.) [See arts. HDr and jnb . But this usage I believe to be post-classical.] ― -b5- [Also (assumed tropical:) A stool; meaning, an evacuation. So in medical books.]
: see majolisN , in two places.

(S, TA.) You say also, jalafa Zuforahu Eano A_iSobaEihi He stripped off his nail from his finger. (Lth, TA.) And accord. to some, jalofN signifies The scraping off, or stripping off, the skin with somewhat of the flesh: and the act of pulling, or drawing, out, or up, or off
; or displacing. (TA.) ― -b2- Also i. q. jarafahu [ He took away, carried away, or removed, the whole of it, or the greater part of it, or much of it

; or he swept it away ]: (K:) or, as some say, jalofN signifies a more intensive and more exterminating action than jarofN . (TA.) ― -b3- And He cut it off; (S;) or pulled it, or plucked it, out, or up

; or eradicated, or uprooted, it; (K;) and exterminated it; (S, K;) as also ↓ . (K.) ― -b4- jalafahu biAls~ayofi He struck him with the sword: (K:) or he cut, or cut a piece from, or cut in pieces, his flesh [ with the sword ]. (A, TA.) ― -b5- julifa Aln~abaAtu The herbage was eaten to the uttermost. (TA.) ― -b6- julifa fiY maAlihi jalofapF He suffered the loss of somewhat of his property, or cattle. (TA.) -A2- jalifa , aor. , inf. n. jalafN and jalaAfapN , (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, rude in disposition, or in make; coarse, or churlish. (K.)

And A^amowaAlahumo ↓ [ It destroyed their cattle ] is also said of a year of great drought, or barrenness, or dearth. (S.) And Ald~ahoru ↓ Time, or fortune, or misfortune, destroyed his property, or cattle. (TA.)

[of mult.] juluwfN (S, M, Msb) and [of pauc.] A^ajolaAfN and A^ajolufN , which last is rare. (Msb.) ― -b2- Also A [ skin of the kind called ] ziq~ without head and without legs. (IAar, K.) ― -b3- And A skinned animal, (AO, S,) or a skinned sheep or goat, (K,) of which the belly has been taken forth, (

(IAth, TA.) ― -b5- Also Thick, or coarse, dry bread: or bread not rendered savoury by anything eaten therewith: or th

, applied to nuwrap [q. v.], That removes hair; (S, K;) as also ↓ . (K.) ― -b2- Applied to a year ( sanapN ), (assumed tropical:) That shaves off, (S,) or nips, shrinks, shrivels, or blasts, [lit., burns, see A^aHoraqa ,] (K,) the plants, or herbage. (S, K.)
, applied to the pubes, Shaven, or having its hair removed, (S, A, K, TA,) by means of nuwrap [q. v.]. (TA.) ― -b2- Applied to a place, (assumed tropical:) [ Shorn of its plants, or herbage
; or] having in it no plants, or herbage. (S, K.) -A2- See also jamuw$N .

senses.text: 1 , (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor. , (Mgh, TA,) inf. n. jamoEN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He collected; brought, or gathered, together; gathered up; assembled; congregated; mustered; drew together

; or contracted; (Mgh, Er-Rághib, B, K; *) a thing; (Er-Rághib, Msb, B;) so that the several parts or portions became near together; (Er-Rághib, B;) or a thing in a scattered, or dispersed, state; (Fr, S;) and a number of men; (Fr;) as also ↓ ; [or this has only an intensive signification;] and ↓ . (TA.) [See also the inf. n., jamoEN , below; and] see 2; and

10. ― -b2- [ jamaEa bayonahumaA He brought them two together, into a state of union, after separation; and particularly, reconciled them; conciliated them: and he, or it, united, connected, or formed a connexion between, them two: see

(TA.) ― -b4- jamaEati AljaAriyapu The girl put on the diroE and the ximaAr and the miloHafap ; (S, TA;) i. e., (tropical:) became a young woman; (S, K, TA;) became full-grown. (TA.) ― -b5- maA jamaEotu biA@moraA^apK qaT~u , and Eani A@moraA^apK , (assumed tropical:) I have never gone in to a woman

(The Lexicons passim.)
2 , (Fr, Msb,) inf. n. tajomiyEN , (K,) He collected; brought, or gathered, together; gathered up; assembled; congregated; mustered; drew together
; or contracted; [thus I render jamaEa , as explained above;] much; with much, or extraordinary, energy, or effectiveness, or the like; vigorously

; or well. (Bd in civ. 2; Msb, K.) Thus in the Kur [civ. 2], Al~a*iY jam~aEa maAlFA waEad~adahu (S, * Bd) Who hath collected much wealth, and hath made it a provision for the casualties of fortune, or reckoned it time after time: (Bd:) [or who hath amassed, or accumulated, wealth, &c.:] or who hath gained, acquired, or earned, wealth, &c.; thus differing from jamaEa , explained above: but it is allowable to say maAlFA ↓ , without teshdeed; (Fr;) and thus it is [generally] read in this passage of the Kur. (Bd.) See also

1. ― -b2- Ham~aEato , (TA,) inf. n. as above, (K,) She (a hen) collected her eggs in her belly. (K, TA.) ― -b3- jam~aEuwA , (inf. n. as above, S,) They were present on the Friday, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or with the congregation [ then collected ], (Mgh,) and performed the prayers [ with the congregation ] on that day. (S, Mgh.) ― -b4- Hence the saying, A^aw~alu jumoEapK jum~iEato fiY AlA_isolaAmu baEoda Almadiynapi bijuw^aAviY [ The first Friday that was observed by the performance of congregational prayer in the time of El-Islám, after the observance thereof in El-Medeeneh, was in Ju-áthà ]. (TA.)

3 , (S, K,) inf. n. mujaAmaEapN (TK) [and jimaAEN ], He combined with him, ( maEahu ↓ , S, K, TA,) and aided him, (TA,) to do such a thing. (S, * K, * TA.) It is said in a trad. of Aboo-Dharr, walaA jimaAEa lanaA fiymaA baEodu i. e. lanaA ↓ [which may mean Nor any combining, or nor any coming together, for us afterwards: see 8]. (TA.) ― -b2- jAmE A@moraA^atahu , (Msb,) inf. n. mujaAmaEapN (S, Msb, K) and jimaAEN , (Mgh, Msb,) (tropical:) He lay with his wife; compressed her. (S, * Mgh, * Msb, K. *) [The latter inf. n. is the more common as meaning Coïtus conjugalis, or the act of compressing ]. -A2- AisotaA^ojara AlA^ajiyra mujaAmaEpF , and jimaAEFA , He hired the hireling for a certain pay every week. (Lh, * TA.)

1. A^ajomaEotu Al$~aYo'a signifies I put the thing together; such, for instance, as spoil, or plunder. (S.) You say, A^ajomaEotu Aln~ahobi , meaning I collected together from every quarter the camels taken as spoil from the people to whom they belonged, and drove them away: (AHeyth:) or A_ijomaAEN signifies [simply] the driving of camels together, or collectively. (K.) ― -b2- AlA_ijomaAEu also signifies The composing and settling a thing which has been discomposed [ and unsettled ]; as an opinion upon which one determines, resolves, or decides: (TA:) or jaEolu AlA^amori jamiyEFA baEoda tafar~uqihi , (AHeyth, K,) i. e. the determining, resolving, or deciding, upon an affair, so as to make it firmly settled, [ after it had been unsettled in the mind, or] after considering what might be its i

62 of the same ch.]. (Bd.) ― -b3- Also The agreeing, or uniting, in opinion. (K, * TA.) You say, A^ajomaEuwA EalaY AlA^amori meaning They agreed, or were of one mind or opinion, upon, or respecting, the affair; (Mgh, Msb;) [and so Ealayohi ↓ ; and Elyh ↓ .] ― -b4- Also The preparing [a thing], or making [it] ready; syn. AlA_iEodaAdu . (K, TA. [In the CK, erroneously, AlAaEodaAdu .]) You say, A^ajomaEotu ka*aA I prepared, or made ready, such a thing. (TA.) And A^ajomiEuwA A^amorakumo Prepare ye for your affair. (Fr.) ― -b5- Also The binding the teats of a she-camel all together with the SiraAr , q. v. (K.) You say, AjmE biAln~aAqapi , (S, TA,) and AjmE Aln~aAqapi , (TA,) He so bound the teats of the she-camel; (S, TA;) and so A^akoma$a bihaA . (TA.) ― -b6- Also The drying [a thing]; drying

8 It (a thing in a scattered or dispersed state, S, and a number of men, Msb, [and a number of things,]) became collected, brought together, gathered together, gathered up, assembled, congregated, mustered, drawn together, or contracted

; or it collected, collected itself together, gathered itself together, came together, assembled, congregated, drew itself together, contracted itself; coalesced; combined; (K, TA;) so that the several parts or portions became near [or close ] together; (TA;) as also AijodamaEa , (K,) with d [substituted for the t ]; (TA;) and ↓ and ↓ signify the same: (Msb, K:) and ↓ signifies they became collected, &c., [ from several places, or] hence and thence. (S, K:) [See also

10.] You say also, AjtmE maEahu (Mgh) and bihi (Msb) [meaning He was, or became, in company with him; came together with him; met with him; met him; had a meeting, or an interview, with him ]. And AjtmE maEahu EalaY A^amori ka*aA : (S, K:) see 3, first sentence: and see the sentence there next following. And in like manner, EalaY ↓ fulaAnK They combined, conspired, or leagued, together against such a one. (Ibn-Buzurj, TA in art. Dfr .) [See also AjtmEwA EalaY AlA^amori in 4, latter half.] You also say, AijotamaEati A=raAw^uhumo EalaY AlA^amori [ Their opinions agreed together, or were in unison, upon, or respecting, the affair ]. (Er-Rághib.) And AijotamaEato $araAy^iTu AlA_imaAmapi The conditions of the office of Imám occurred together [or were combined, or they coexisted, in such a case]
10 ↓ [ He desired, or demanded, the collecting together of every body of soldiers

; or he summoned together every body of soldiers ]: said of him who demands, or summons, armies, or military forces. (S, TA.) [But this usage of the verb is perhaps post-classical: for Mtr says,] With respect to the saying of ElAbeewardee, $aA=miy~apN tasotajomiEu Al$~awola Harojafu [ A north wind, cold and vehement, inviting to collect themselves together the she-camels whose milk has dried up, they having passed seven or eight months since bringing forth, or since pregnancy ], it seems that he has compared this verb with the generality of others of the same class, [and so derived the meaning in which he has here used it,] or that he heard it [in that sense] from the people of the cities, or towns, or villages, and cultivated lands. (Mgh.) -A2- AstjmE used intransitively is syn. with Ajtm
1. (S, &c.) [Hence,] yawomu AljamoEi The day of resurrection [when all mankind will be collected together]. (IDrd, K.) ― -b2-

Also, without the article Al , A name of El-Muzdelifeh [between 'Arafát and Minè]; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) determinate, like EarafaAtu : (TA:) so called because people collect themselves there; (S, Msb;) or because Adam there met with Eve (Mgh, Msb) after they had fallen [from Paradise]: (TA:) [or, app., a name of the tract from 'Arafát to Minè inclusive of these two places: and hence,] yawomu jamoEK the day of 'Arafeh [when the pilgrims halt at Mount 'Arafát]: and A^ay~aAmu jamoEK the days of Minè. (IDrd, K.) ― -b3- As an inf. n. used as a subst., properly so termed, (S, * Mgh, Msb,) it also signifies A collection; a number together; an assembly; a company, troop, congregated or collective body, party, or group; a mass; syn. ↓ , (S, Mgh, L, Msb, K,) of men; (S, L, K;) as also ↓ (L, Msb, TA) and

(TA.) And jaA='a fulaAnN biquboDapK milo'K jumoEihi Such a one came with a quantity in his grasp as much as filled his clinched hand. (S, TA.) 778.) ― -b2- A^axa*otu fulaAnFA bijumoEi viyaAbihi , (S, Msb, *) and ↓ viyaAbihi , (Msb,) i. e. [ I took, or seized, such a one ] by the part where his garments met together. (Msb.) ― -b3- A^amoruhumo bijumoEi , and ↓ , (tropical:) Their affair, or case, is concealed, (S, K,) undivulged by them, and unknown by any one [ beside them ]. Hence, (Mgh,) yawomu AljumoEapi , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) the original form, (TA,) of the dial. of 'Okeyl; (Msb, TA;) and yawomu AljumuEapi , (S, Msb, K,) the most chaste form, (TA,) of the dial. of El-Hijáz; (Msb, TA;) and yawomu AljumaEapi , (Msb, K,) of the dial. of Benoo-Temeem; (Msb, TA;) and, in consequence of frequency of usage, AljumaEapu alone; (Mgh;) A well-known day; (K;) [ the day of the congregation; i. e. Friday; ] formerly called (TA) the day of AlEaruwbap : (S, TA:) called ywm AljmEp because of the congregating of the people thereon: (Msb:) Th asserts that the first who named it thus was Kaab Ibn-Lu-eí; and he is related to have said that it was thus called because Kureysh used to gather themselves together to Kuseí, [on that day,] in [the building called] daAru Aln~adowapi : (TA
; or a collection of things]; (K;) as in the phrase jumoEapN mino HaSFY [ a collection of pebbles ]. (TA.) ― -b6- You say also jumoEapN mino tamorK , meaning A handful of dates. (S, K.)
[ Of, or relating to, a plural. ]
One who fasts on Friday by himself. (IAar, Th.)

: see jamoEN as signifying “ a plural, ” in three places. [The primary signification seems to be the last there mentioned; where it is said,] AljimaAEu is What comprises a number [of things]: (S, K:) one says, Alxamoru jimaAEu AlA_ivomi (S, TA) [i. e. Wine is what comprises a number of sins: or] that in which sin is comprised, and known to be: the saying is a trad.: (TA:) or jimaAEu AlA_ivomi signifies the plurality ( jamoE ) of sins. (Msb.) Hence also the saying of El-Hasan El-Basree, Ait~aquwA h`*ihi AlA^ahowaA='a faA_in~a jimaAEahaA AlD~alaAlapu wamaEaAdahaA Aln~aAru [ Beware ye of these natural desires; for what they involve is error, and the place to which they lead is the fire of Hell]. (TA: in the L, wmyEAdhA .) And it is said in a trad., Had~ivoniY bikalimapK takuwnu jimaAEFA i. e.

; or, accord. to the A, that comprises a sheep or goat: (TA:) or a great cooking-pot; (S, K;) as also ↓ : (Sgh, K:) pl. [most probably of this last] jumoEN [like as buzolN is pl. of baAzilN , &c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- [ All, or the whole, of any things or thing.] See A^ajomaEu , last sentence. ― -b3- [As an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant,] A tribe [or any number of men ] in a state of collection, congregation, or union; being together; met together; syn. ↓ . (TA.) ― -b5- rajulN jamiyEN

and ↓ [are mentioned together, but not explained, in the TA: the former signifies, and probably, judging from analogy, the latter likewise, as also ↓ , One who collects much

Anything of which the several component parts are collected, brought, gathered, or drawn, together. (IDrd, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] as an epithet, applied to a woman, it means Short. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] jum~aAEN Alv~uray~aA The cluster of the Pleiades: (IDrd:) or persons who collect together for the rain of the Pleiades, which is the rain called AlwasomiY~ , looking for the fruitfulness and herbage resulting from it. (IAar.) ― -b4- And jum~aAEu Aln~aAsi A medley, or mixed or promiscuous multitude or collection, of men, or people, (S, Msb, K,) of various tribes; (S, K;) as also jum~aAEN alone: (TA:) or the latter, people scattered, or in a state of dispersion. (Ham p.

302.) ― -b5- jum~aAEN also signifies The place [either properly or tropically] which comprises the origin of anything; (K, TA;) the source of descent or extraction of people; and hence applied by I 'Ab to main tribes from which other tribes are derived

; or, as some say, used by him as meaning various classes of men, such as are termed A^awozaAE and A^awo$aAb . (TA.) ― -b6- [And The main, or most essential, part of a thing. Thus,] jum~aAEu jasadi AlA_inosaAni means The head of the man. (TA.) ― -b7- jum~aAEu Alt~amori The contraction ( tajam~uE ) of the envelopes of the flowers of dates, in one place, upon [ the germs of ] the fruit, or produce, thereof. (TA.)

[act. part. n. of 1; Collecting; &c.] ― -b2- AljaAmiEu one of the names of God; meaning The Collector of the created beings for the day of reckoning: or, as some say, the Combiner of things of similar natures and of things of contrary natures, in existence. (IAth.) ― -b3- The belly; [because it collects what passes from the stomach;] of the dial. of El-Yemen. (TA.) ― -b4-

Also, (Msb,) or Almasojidu AljaAmiEu , (S, K,) [ The congregational mosque; ] the mosque in which the [ congregational ] prayers of Friday are performed; because it collects the people for a certain time; (Msb;) and you may also say, masojidu AljaAmiEi , meaning masojidu Alyawomi AljaAmiEi , (S, K,) like as you say AlHaq~u Alyaqiynu and Haq~u Alyaqiyni , [the latter] as meaning Haq~u Al$~aYo'i Alyaqiyni ; for it is not allowable to prefix a noun to another of the same meaning except with this kind of subaudition

; or, accord. to Fr, the Arabs used to do so because of the difference of the two words themselves: (S:) or msjd AljAmE is a mistake: (K:) so says Lth; but all others allow it; for the Arabs prefix a subst. to another signifying the same thing, and also to its epithet, as in the phrases in the Kur diynu Alqay~imapi [ch. xcviii. v. 4] and waEoda AlS~idoqi [ch. xlvi. v. 15]: (Az, TA:) [pl. jawaAmiEu .] ― -b5- miSorN jaAmiEN [ A great town comprising a large population; a comprehensive great town ]. (Msb in art. mdn [where it is given as the explanation of madiynapN ]; and K in art. qrY [where it is less properly given as the explanation of qaroyapN ].) ― -b6- qidorN jaAmiEN and jaAmiEapN : see jimaAEN ― -b7- AimoraA^apN jAmiEN : see the paragraph commencing with AljumoEu ; last signification

[ Collecting, comprising, or containing, a greater, or the greatest, number or quantity; more, or most, comprehensive. Of its usage in a superlative sense, the following are exs.]. A_i*aA A^axa*a $aAhida zuwrK baEava bihi A_ilaY Als~uwqi A^ajomaEa maA kaAna [ When he took a false witness, he sent him to the market when it comprised, or contained, the greatest number of people]: AjmE being here in the accus. case as a denotative of state with respect to the swq : and the reason why kAnt is not here said [instead of kAn ] is that swq is sometimes masc. (Mgh.) And AifoEalo maA huwa A^ajomaEu liA^uSuwli AlA^aHokaAmi [ Do thou that which is most comprehensive in relation to the principles of the ordinances applying to the case]. (Msb in art. HwT .) -A2- [As a simple epithet, Entire, complete, o

; or it is jamaAEaY ; it is not jumoEN , because A^ajomaEu is not an epithet, like as A^aHomaru is, of which the pl. is HumorN ; (L;) for it is determinate, though of the measure of an epithet, which is indeterminate; (AAF;) and though it is in concordance with the noun which precedes it, like an epithet, it is shown to be not an epithet by its not having a broken pl.: (L:) it is a simple corroborative; (S, K;) and so are A^ajomaEuwna and jamoEaA='u and jumaEu ; not used as an inchoative nor as an enunciative nor as the agent of a verb nor as the objective complement of a verb, like as are some other corroboratives, such as nafosuhu and Eayonuhu and kul~uhu . and majomiEN , (S, Msb, K,) the latter anomalous, like ma$oriqN and magoribN &c., (TA,) A place of collecting, and the like: (S, Msb, * K:) [pl. majaAmiEu ] [Hence,] majomaEu AlbaHorayoni , in the Kur [xviii. 59], means The place where the two seas meet. [act. part. n. of 1]. You say A=fapN jaAy^iHapN A destructive bane or pest or the like: (Msb:) and sanapN jaAy^iHapN a year of drought or dearth or sterility: (Mgh:) pl. jawaAy^iHu . (Mgh, Msb.) ― -b2- [And hence,] The locust. (IAar, T in art. jHY .)

[fem. of jaAy^iHN , q. v.: and hence, as a subst.,] A bane, a pest, (Msb,) a calamity, or the like, (S, Msb, K,) or a great calamity, (Mgh, TA,) that destroys, or extirpates, men's property, or cattle; (S, Mgh, Msb, * K, TA;) as drought, or dearth

; or civil war, or conflict and faction, and the like: (S, TA:) drought, or dearth, that destroys, or extirpates, men's property, or cattle; as also ↓ : (Wásil, TA:) or a calamity that befalls a man, and destroys all his property, or cattle: (A'Obeyd, T:) or severe drought or dearth, that destroys, or extirpates, men's property, or cattle: (ISh:) sometimes it is the effect of large hail; and sometimes, of excessive cold or heat: (T:) or (accord. to Esh-Sháfi'ee, Mgh, Msb) a blast, or blight, or calamity arising from the atmosphere, that destroys the fruits, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) or some thereof; (Mgh;) only relating to fruits: (TA:) pl. jawaAy^iHu . (A, Mgh, Msb.) It is said in a trad., A^amara biwaDoEi AljawaAy^iHi , which is an elliptical phrase, meaning He commanded to remit the poor-rate in
: see what next follows.
Property, or cattle, destroyed by a bane, or pest, or the like; as also majiyHN [belonging to art. jyH ], and ↓ . (Msb.)
[A person or thing] that destroys, or extirpates, everything. (K, TA.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. yajuwdu , inf. n. juwdapN and jawodapN , It (a thing, S, or a commodity, an article of household-goods, or the like, Msb, and a work, or performance, TA) was, or became, jay~id [i. e. good, goodly, approvable, or excellent; the verb being the contr. of raduw^a , as is implied in the A and K]: (S, A, Msb, K:) in this sense, accord. to some, of the class of qaAla ; accord. to others, of the class of qaruba . (Msb.) [Also said of a man, meaning He was, or became, excellent, or egregious, in some quality; sometimes, though very rarely, in a quality that is disapproved.] ― -b2- And jAd , (S, A, Msb, K,) of the class of qAl , (Msb,) aor. as above, (S, Msb,) inf. n. juwdN , (S, A, Msb, K,) with damm, (S, Msb,) He was liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous: (K:) or he affected, or co

Hence, (Msb,) jAd binafosihi , (S, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (S, A,) inf. n. jawodN (TA) and juw^uwdN , (S, TA,) (tropical:) He gave up his spirit, (A, Msb, TA,) at death; (S, Msb;) like as one gives away his property; said of one in the agony of death: (TA:) and (tropical:) he gave away his life, in war. (Msb.) And you say also, jaAdato nafosuhu (assumed tropical:) [ His soul, or spirit, resigned itself, or departed ]. (Msb in art. nfs .) ― -b4- jAd AlmaTaru , inf. n. jawodN , The rain was, or became, copious, or abundant. (S.) And jaAdati Als~amaA='u , (A, Msb,) inf. n. jawodN , with fet-h, The sky rained. (Msb.) And jaAdati AlEayonu , inf. n. jawodN and juw^uwdN , The eye shed many, or abundant, tears. (Lh, K.) ― -b5- jAd said of a horse, (S, A, L, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (S,) inf. n. juw

3. ― -b2- jaAdahumo , aor. yajuwdu , inf. n. jawodN , It (rain) rained, or descended, upon them copiously, or abundantly. (L.) And jiyduwA They were rained upon with a copious, or an abundant, rain. (L.) And jiydati AlA^aroDu , (S, L, K,) inf. n. jawodN ; (As, TA;) and ↓ ; (K;) The earth, or land, was rained upon with a copious, or an abundant, rain: (S, L, K:) or, so that the moisture of the rain met that of the soil. (As, TA.) ― -b3- jiyda , (S, A, K,) aor. yujaAdu , (S, K,) inf. n. juwaAdN , (S, * K, * TA,) (assumed tropical:) He (a man, S, A) thirsted, or became affected by thirst: (S, A, K:) or thirsted vehemently: (accord. to an explanation of juwaAdN in the K:) or was at the point of death, or destruction; (K;) as though destruction rained upon him. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence,] A_in~iY A^u

Also, app., jyda , aor. yujaAdu , inf. n. juwaAdN , (as in a sense explained above,) (assumed tropical:) He became affected, or overcome, or distressed, (see majuwdN ,) by drowsiness, or slumber: for] juwaAdN is syn. with nuEaAsN : (L, TA:) and you say, jAdhu Aln~uEaAsu (assumed tropical:) Drowsiness, or slumber, overcame him; (L;) as though sleep rained upon him. (TA.)
2 see 4: ― -b2- and see also

3 He vied with him, or contended with him for superiority, in liberality, bounty, munificence, or generosity. (S, TA.) You say, jAwdhu ↓ He vied with him, or contended &c., in liberality, &c., and overcame him therein. (TA.)

4 He made it good, goodly, approvable, or excellent; (S, A, * K;) as also A^ajowadahu , (S, * K,) like as they said ATAl and ATwl , and AHAl and AHwl , and ATAb and ATyb , and AlAn and Alyn ; (S;) and ↓ , (S, * A,) inf. n. tajowiydN . (S.) [Hence,] AjAdhu Aln~aqoda He gave him the cash, or ready money, good. (S, K.) And A^ajadotuka vawobFA I gave thee a garment, or piece of cloth, that was good, goodly, or excellent
; or in a good state. (A, TA.) ― -b2- He gave him a dirhem, or piece of silver. (K.) ― -b3- A^ujiydati AlA^aroDu : see

1. -A2- He, or it, slew him, or killed him. (L.) -A3- AjAd , (inf. n. A_ijaAdapN , Msb,) He said, gave utterance to, uttered, or expressed, what was good, approvable, or excellent; he said, or did, well, or excellently; A^ataY biAljay~idi (L, Msb, K) mino qawoli A^awo fiEolK ; (Msb;) as also A^ajowada ; (L;) and ↓ , inf. n. jawodapN . (L.) [You say, qaAla faA^ajaAda He said, and said well: and faEala faA^ajaAda He did, and did well. ] And AjAd fiY Eamalihi , and Ajwd , He did well, or excellently, in his work. (L.) ― -b2- Said of a horse, and Ajwd likewise: see

1. ― -b3- Also He had with him a horse such as is termed jawaAd [i. e. fleet, or swift, and excellent ]: (S:) or he became possessed of such a horse; (A, K;) as also Ajwd . (K.) ― -b4- A^ajaAdato She brought forth a child, or children, of liberal, bountiful, or generous, disposition. (A.) And AjAd biAlwaladi He begot the child, or children, of liberal, bountiful, or generous, disposition; (K;) and in like manner, bihi A^abawaAhu ↓ [ His two parents so engendered him ]. (TA.)
5 He chose what was good, goodly, approvable, or excellent, among all things. (Ham p.
299.) He affected nicety, or refinement; he was, or became, nice, exquisite, refined, or scrupulously nice and exact

; or he chose what was excellent, or best, to be done; and exceeded the usual bounds; fiY SanoEatihi in his work of art, or his manufacture; syn. tanaw~aqa . (A, TA.) And tjw~d wabaAlaga fiY maToEamihi wamalobasihi [ He was dainty, nice, exquisite, refined, or scrupulously nice and exact

; or he chose what was excellent, or best; and exceeded the usual bounds; in his food and his apparel ]; (JK and K in art. nwq ;) he was studious of his diet and apparel, always eating exquisite food and wearing sumptuous clothing. (TK in that art.) -A2- tjw~dhu : see
10. tajaw~adotuhaA laka I chose, or selected, the best, or most excellent, (↓ ,) thereof for thee. (TA.)

6 They considered [or tried ] which of them had the best argument, or plea, or allegation: (K, TA:) so says Aboo-Sa'eed on the authority of an Arab of the desert. (TA.) And yatajaAwaduwna AlHadiyva They consider, or see, [or try, ] which of them will be best in narration, or talk, or discourse. (A.) ― -b2- [Also They vied, or contended together for superiority, in liberality, bounty, munificence, or generosity. ]

10 He reckoned it, or esteemed it, good, goodly, approvable, or excellent: (S:) or he found it to be so: (K:) or he desired, or sought, that it might be so, (A, K,) and chose it, or selected it; (A;) as also ↓ . (A.) You say also, Aisotajowada raA^oyahu [ He esteemed his judgment, or opinion, good: or found it to be so ]. (TA in art. jzl .) ― -b2- He desired, or sought, or demanded, his liberality, bounty, munificence, or generosity. (K.) ― -b3- He desired, or sought, that he (a horse) might be such as is termed jawaAd [i. e. fleet, or swift, and excellent ]. (K.) -A2- AstjAd It came or happened, well. (KL.)

Copious, or abundant, rain; (S, L, K;) as also ↓ : (S:) or rain that thoroughly irrigates everything: (M:) or rain that is not exceeded: (M, L, K:) accord. to some, who observe that the phrase, mentioned by Sb, A^axa*otanaA biAljawodiwafawoqhaA [ Thou hast assailed us with a storm of reproach or the like not to be exceeded, and with that which is above it, ] is one of hyperbole and reproach. (M, L.) It is an inf. n. thus used as an epithet [and therefore applicable without variation to a fem. as to a masc. n., and to a dual and a pl. as to a sing. n.]: (L:) and is also pl. [or rather a quasi-pl. n.] of jaAy^idN , (S, L, K,) like as SaHobN is of SaAHibN . (S, L.) You say maTarN jawodN [ A copious, or an abundant, rain; &c.]: (L:) and saHaAbapN jawodN [ A cloud yielding a copious, or an abun
; or it may be pl. of tajowaAdN [an inf. n.]. (L.) You say also, AmaTari ↓ [ Copious showers of rain fell upon him, or it ]. (A.) ― -b2- See also jawaAdN .
[an inf. n. of 1, (q. v.,) in two senses; as also juwdapN : and an inf. n. of un., signifying] A single affection of thirst; a thirsting. (S, K.) ― -b2- See also juwaAdN .
Saffron. (S, K.)

, used alike as masc. and fem., (S, K,) Liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous: (S, * K:) or one who affects, or constrains himself, to be generous: (Msb:) or who gives without being asked, to preserve the receiver from the ignominy of asking: (MF:) or who gives what is meet to him to whom it is meet: (El-Karmánee, TA:) or who gives what is meet to him to whom it is meet, not for a compensation; so that it has a more special signification than muHosinN : (MF:) pl. [of pauc., masc.,] A^ajowaAdN and (of mult., TA) juwodN , (S, A, K,) like as qu*ulN is pl. of qa*aAlN , but the w is made quiescent because it is an unsound letter, (S,) [in some copies of the K juwudN ,] and A^ajaAwidu , (S, K,) contr. to analogy, (TA,) or A^ajaAwiydu , [reg., as pl. of A^ajowaAdN ,] (A,) and juwadaA='u (S,
Also, applied alike to the male and the female, (S,) A courser; a fleet, or swift, and excellent, horse; (L;) a horse fleet, or swift, in running

; or excellent in running, or in the motion of his legs; as also ↓ : (Bd in xxxviii. 30:) or that outstrips others: (Jel ib.:) i. q. raAy^iEN : (S, L, K:) pl. jiyaAdN , (S, A, Bd, L, Msb, K,) which by rule should be jiwaAdN , like TiwaAlN , but this latter form has not been heard from the Arabs; (L;) or jiyaAdN is pl. of jawodN , or of jay~idN ; (Bd ubi suprá;) and jawaAdN has also for its pl. A^ajoyaAdN , [a pl. of pauc., and irregular, or this is pl. of jay~dN , and therefore, though irregularly, retains the Y substituted for w ] (S, L,) and A^ajowaAdN , [also a pl. of pauc., but agreeable with rule, or this is pl. of jawodN ,] (L,) and A^ajaAwiydu (S, L) is pl. of A^ajowaAdN . (L.)

Hence, A^aqobala jawaAdFA (assumed tropical:) He came on, or advanced, like a horse that is termed jwAd : and sirotu A_ilayohi jawaAdFA (assumed tropical:) I went to him, or it, like a horse that is so termed. (Mgh in art. g* .) You say also, EadaA EadowFA jawaAdFA He ran a long run. (A, TA.) And sironaA EuqobapF jawaAdFA , and Euqobatayoni jawaAdayoni , and EuqabFA jiyaAdFA (S, A) and A^ajowaAdFA , (A, TA,) We journeyed a long march or stage, and two long marches or stages, and long marches or stages. (S, A, TA.)
[accord. to the TA inf. n. of jiyda , which see in two places,] (assumed tropical:) Thirst: (S, K:) or vehemence of thirst. (K.) ― -b2-
Also, [accord. to the K ↓ , but this is corrected in the TA,] (assumed tropical:) Drowsiness, or slumber. (TA.)

, originally of the measure fayoEilN , (S, Msb,) as the Basrees say, i. e. jayowidN , (Msb, TA,) the w being changed into Y because of its being meksoor and preceded by Y , and the augmentative Y being then incorporated into it; (TA;) or, as the Koofees say, of the measure fayoEalN , like EayoTalN &c., because there is found no sound word of the measure fayoEilN except SayoqilN , a woman's name, and the unsound is accorded to the sound

; or, as others say, of the measure faEiylN , [and so I find in one copy of the S,] originally jawiydN , the kesreh of the w being, accord. to them, suppressed because difficult of pronunciation, and the quiescent w and Y thus coming together, [the latter receives the rejected kesreh, and] the w is changed into Y and incorporated into the [augmentative] Y ; (Msb;) Good, goodly, approvable, or excellent; contr. of radi Yo ; (A, K;) applied to a thing, (S,) or a commodity, an article of household-goods, or the like, (A, Msb,) and a work, or performance: (TA:) pl. jiyaAdN (S, A, Msb, K) and jiyaAdaAtN , (K,) the latter a pl. pl., [i. e. pl. of jiyaAdN ,] (TA,) and jayaAy^idu , (S, K,) with hemz, [and, accord. to some,] contr. to analogy. (S.) [It is also applied to a man, meaning Excellent, o
[ Better, and best; more, and most, goodly or approvable or excellent ]: see

5. ― -b2- [ More, and most, liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous. Hence,] A^ajowadu mino HaAtimK [ More liberal, &c., than Hátim ]: a prov. (Meyd.) ― -b3- [ More, and most, fleet, or swift, and excellent; relating to a horse. Hence,] A^ajowadu mina AljawaAdi Almubir~i [ More fleet, &c., than the courser that surpasses others ]: a prov. (Meyd.)
: see jawodN , in two places.

A field, or garden, rained upon: (A:) [or rained upon copiously, or abundantly. ] And A^aroDN majowdapN Land rained upon with a copious, or an abundant, rain. (S, L, K.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) A man (S, A) affected with thirst: (S, A, K:) [or, with vehement thirst: (see juwaAdN :)] or at the point of death, or destruction. (K.) ― -b3- And [hence,] (tropical:) Affected with longing desire. (L.) ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) Overcome by drowsiness, or slumber: (TA:) or distressed by drowsiness, or slumber, &c. (Lh, L.)

: see mijowaAdN . ― -b2- Also A man possessing a horse such as is termed jawaAdi [i. e. fleet, or swift, and excellent ]: pl. majaAwiydu [by rule pl. of mijowaAdN , q. v.]. (A, TA.) ― -b3- HatofN mujiydN (tropical:) Present death. (K, TA.)

One who says, utters, or expresses, or who does, (K, TA,) much, or often, (TA,) what is good, goodly, approvable, or excellent; (K, TA;) as also ↓ : (TA:) [or rather the latter is a simple, not an intensive, epithet:] the former is applied to a poet, (S, A, K,) as syn. with the latter, (K,) or as meaning who says, or utters, much, or often, what is good, or excellent: (S:) and both are applied to a workman, or an artificer: pl. of the former majaAwiydu . (A.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. yajuwru , (TA,) inf. n. jaworN , (S, A, K,) He declined, or deviated, from the right course; (S, A;) and so jArEani AlqaSodi : (A:) he wandered from the right way: (TA:) he pursued a wrong course: (K:) or he left the right way in journeying: and it (anything) declined. (TA.) You say also, jAr Eani AlT~iriyqi He declined, or deviated, from the road, or way. (S, Mgh, Msb.) ― -b2- And jAr , (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor. as above, (Msb,) and so the inf. n., (Mgh, Msb, K,) He acted wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically, (S, * Mgh, Msb, K,) Ealayohi against him, (S, TA,) fiY Hukomihi in his judgment, (Msb,) or fiY AlHukomi in judgment. (S, TA.) ― -b3- jArti AlA^aroDu (tropical:) The plants, or herbage, of the land grew tall: (A, TA:) and so jaA^arat . (TA.) -A2- See also

2 , (S, A, K,) inf. n. tajowiyrN , (S,) He attributed, or imputed, to him, or charged him with, or accused him of, wrongful, unjust, injurious, or tyrannical, conduct; (S, K;) contr. of Ead~alahu . (A.) -A2- He prostrated him (S, K) by a blow, (S,) or by a thrust of a spear or the like; from jAr “he, or it, declined;”; (A;) like kaw~arahu . (S.) ― -b2- He threw it down, (TA,) and overturned it; (K, TA;) namely, a building, and a tent, &c.: (TA:) he took it to pieces; namely, a tent. (A.)

3 , inf. n. mujaAwarapN and jiwaArN (S, Msb, K) and ↓ , (S, M, and some copies of the K,) or the last is a simple subst., (Msb,) and ↓ , (M, and so in some copies of the K instead of juwaArN ,) of which forms the second ( jiwaArN ) is more chaste than the third (S, TA) and than the fourth, as relating to the verb in the sense here following, though some disapprove of it, and assert the third and the fourth to be more chaste; (TA;) He became his jAr [or neighbour ]; (K;) he lived in his neighbourhood, or near to him: (Msb, TA:) or he lived in a dwelling contiguous to his. (Msb.) ― -b2- Also jAwrhu , (TA,) inf. n. jiwaArN , (K,) and ↓ is said to be a quasi-inf. n., and more chaste than jiwaArN as relating to the verb in the sense here following; (TA;) He bound himself to him by a covenant to

4 , (S, A, &c.,) inf. n. A_ijaArapN (Mgh, K) and ↓ , (Kr, K,) [or the latter is rather a quasi-inf. n., like TaAEapN from A^aTaAEahu ,] He protected him; granted him refuge; (K;) preserved, saved, rescued, or liberated, him; (S, A, Msb, K;) from ( mino ) wrongful, unjust, injurious, or tyrannical, treatment; (S, K;) from punishment; (S, A;) or from what he feared: (Msb:) he aided him; succoured him; delivered him from evil: the A^a having a privative effect. (Mgh.) It is said of God, yujiyru walaA yujaAru Ealayohi He protects, but none is protected against him. (TA.) And in the Kur [lxxii. 22], qulo A_in~iY lano yujiyraniY mina A@ll~`hi A^aHadN Verily none will protect me against God. (TA.) ― -b2- AjAr AlmataAEa He put the household-goods, or commodities, into the repository, (K, TA,) and

5 He became prostrated; (S;) he fell down; (K;) by reason of a blow. (S, TA.) ― -b2- It (a building, TA) became thrown down, or demolished. (K.) ― -b3- He (a man, TA) laid himself down on his side (K) upon his bed. (TA.)

6 and ↓ (S, K) are syn., (S,) signifying They became mutual neighbours; they lived near together: (K, * TA:) the [radical] w in the latter verb remaining unaltered because this verb is syn. with one in which the w must preserve its original form on account of the quiescence of the preceding letter, namely, tjAwrwA , (S, TA,) and to show that it is syn. therewith: but AijotaAruwA also occurs. (TA.) ― -b2- [Also They bound themselves by a covenant to protect one another. ]

10 and ↓ , (K,) the latter like jaArN as syn. with musotajiyrN , (TA,) He sought, desired, or asked, to be protected; to be granted refuge; to be preserved, saved, rescued, or liberated. (K.) And AstjArhu He desired him, or asked him, to preserve, save, rescue, or deliver, him, (S, A, Msb,) mino fulaAnK from such a one. (S.) And AstjAr bihi He had recourse to him for refuge, protection, or preservation; he sought his protection. (TA.)

A neighbour; one who lives near to another; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) one who lives in the next tent or house: (IAar, Th, T, Msb:) pl. [of mult.] jiyraAnN (Msb, K) [and jiwaArN (a pl. not of unfrequent occurrence, and mentioned by Freytag as used by El-Mutanebbee,)] and [of pauc.] jiyrapN and A^ajowaArN ; (K;) like qaAEN , pl. qiyEaAnN and qiyEapN and A^aqowaAEN , the only similar instance: (TA:) fem. with p . (Mgh.) AljaAru *uw AlqurobaY [in the Kur iv. 40] is The relation, or kinsman, who is abiding in one's neighbourhood: or who is abiding in one town or district or the like while thou art in another, and who has that title to respect which belongs to nearness of relationship: (TA:) or the near neighbour: (Bd, Jel:) or the near relation: (Jel:) or he who is near, and connected, by relationship

, an inf. n. used as an epithet, (TA,) i. q. ↓ ; (K, TA;) i. e. Declining, or deviating, from the right course: and acting wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically: (TA:) pl. [of the latter], applied to men, ↓ , (K,) in which the w remains unaltered contr. to rule, (TA,) and ↓ , (A, K,) as in all the copies of the K, but some substitute for it, as a correction, ↓ , [found in a copy of the A,] which, however, requires consideration, (TA,) and jaAy^iruwna . (K.) You say TariyqN jaworN A road, or way, deviating from the right course. (TA.) And huwa jaworN Eano TariyqinaA He is declining, or deviating, from our way. (TA.) ― -b2-

Also, for *uw jawor , meaning Wronged, or unjustly treated, by the judge. (Mgh from a trad.) ― -b3- Einodahu mina AlmaAli Aljaworu (tropical:) He possesses, of property, an extraordinary abundance. (A, TA.) See also jiwar~N .
: see jaArN , in three places: -A2- and jaworN : -A3- and see also
and juwarapN : see jaworN .
Verily he is good in respect of the mode, or manner, of jiwaAr [i. e. living as a neighbour, or binding himself by covenant to protect others ]. (TA.)

A rain accompanied by vehement thunder: (K:) or by a vehement sound of thunder: (S:) or a copious rain; as also jaA^orN and juw^arN ; (K in art. jA^r ;) and, accord. to As, juw^aArN : (TA:) and an exceedingly great torrent. (TA. [In this last sense written in a copy of the A ↓ , and there said to be tropical.]) See jawaArN : and see also art. jr . ― -b2- You say also baAzilN jiwar~N (S) [app. meaning A camel nine years old that brays loudly: or] hard and strong: and baEiyrN jiwar~N a bulky camel. (TA.)

3. -A2- Also The part of the exterior court or yard of a house that is coextensive with the house. (K, * TA.) -A3- Abundant and deep water. (K.) Whence ↓ applied to rain. (TA.) -A4- Ships: a dial. var. of jawaArK ; on the authority of Sá'id, (K,) surnamed Abu-l-'Alà: (TA:) said in the K to be strange; but similar instances are well known. (MF.)
: see 3, in two places. ― -b2-
Also, and ↓ , or the latter is only an inf. n., The covenant between two parties by which either is bound to protect the other. (TA.)
: see what next precedes. -A2- [Also a pl. of jaArN .]
: see jaworN . ― -b2- Also (tropical:) Wide and big; applied to a [bucket of the kind called] garob : and so, with p , applied to a [skin of the kind called] qirobap . (A, TA.)

[as meaning Thrown down, or overturned, ] occurs in the following prov.: yawomN biyawomi AlHafaDi Almujaw~ari [ A day for a day of the household-goods (or, accord. to the TA, the hair-cloth tent ) thrown down, or overturned ]: applied in the case of rejoicing at a calamity befalling another: a man had an aged paternal uncle, and used continually to go into the latter's tent, or house, and throw down his household-goods, one upon another; and when he himself grew old, sons of a brother of his did to him as he had done to his paternal uncle; wherefore he said thus, meaning, this is for what I did to my paternal uncle. (K.)
